Search and filtering parameters for order item retrieval operations within specific orders.

Provides comprehensive search capabilities for order items belonging to a particular order, including text search across product names and attributes, quantity ranges, price filters, seller-specific filtering, and flexible sorting options. The parameters support complex filtering scenarios while maintaining performance through proper pagination.

Security considerations include ensuring that search operations only return order items belonging to orders that the authenticated user is authorized to access. All filtering is applied within the context of the parent order specified in the endpoint path, preventing unauthorized access to order items from other orders.

The filtering system integrates with the shopping_mall_order_items table from the Prisma schema, incorporating all available fields for comprehensive search functionality. Each filter parameter corresponds directly to database fields, ensuring efficient query performance and accurate result matching.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the payment record.

Unique UUID v4 identifier automatically generated when the payment record is created. Serves as the immutable reference for all payment-related operations and audit trails.

The ID ensures each payment transaction can be uniquely identified and tracked throughout its complete lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Credit card payment method for secure transaction processing.
PayPal digital payment method for online transactions.
Bank transfer payment method for direct bank transactions.
Digital wallet payment method for mobile and online payments.

payment_method.description:
Payment method used for the transaction, supporting credit cards, PayPal, bank transfers, and digital wallets.

Specifies the payment mechanism selected for processing the transaction. Each method has specific security requirements, processing workflows, and customer experience considerations.

The method determines gateway compatibility, transaction fees, processing timelines, and regulatory compliance requirements.

payment_gateway.description:
Payment gateway service used for processing the transaction.

Identifies the specific payment processing service that handles transaction authorization, capture, and settlement. Gateway selection depends on payment method compatibility, regional availability, and business partnerships.

The gateway manages secure communication with financial institutions, fraud detection, and transaction reconciliation processes.

transaction_id.description:
Unique transaction identifier provided by the payment gateway.

External reference ID generated by the payment gateway that uniquely identifies this transaction in their system. Essential for cross-referencing, dispute resolution, and financial reconciliation.

The transaction ID serves as the primary link between internal payment records and external payment processor systems.

amount.description:
Total amount processed for this payment transaction in the specified currency.

The monetary value of the payment representing the amount charged to the customer. Must be positive and comply with currency-specific formatting and validation rules.

The amount influences processing fees, gateway selection, tax calculations, and financial reporting requirements.

currency.description:
Currency code for the payment transaction using ISO 4217 standard format.

Three-letter currency code specifying the monetary unit for the transaction (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW). Determines formatting, exchange rates, and regional compliance requirements.

The currency must be supported by the selected payment gateway and align with business rules for international transactions.

oneOf.description: Payment is awaiting authorization or initial processing.
Payment has been authorized but not yet captured.
Payment has been successfully captured and funds are transferred.
Payment authorization was declined by the payment processor.
Payment has been partially or fully refunded to the customer.
Payment is under dispute investigation by the customer or processor.
Payment has been charged back by the customer's financial institution.

status.description:
Current status of the payment transaction throughout its lifecycle.

Tracks the progression of the payment from initial authorization through completion, refund, or dispute resolution. Status transitions follow business rules and regulatory requirements.

The status provides real-time visibility into payment processing and enables appropriate workflow actions based on current state.

authorization_code.description:
Payment authorization code provided by the payment gateway.

Unique code generated during the authorization phase that serves as proof of initial payment approval. Required for capture operations and essential for audit trails.

The authorization code validates that the payment has passed initial security checks and is ready for fund transfer.

captured_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the payment was successfully captured.

Records the exact date and time when funds were transferred from the customer's account to the merchant's account. Uses ISO 8601 format for consistent timestamp representation.

The capture timestamp is essential for financial reporting, reconciliation, and customer service operations.

refunded_amount.description:
Total amount that has been refunded from this payment transaction.

Tracks the cumulative refund amount processed for this payment. Must not exceed the original payment amount and supports partial refund scenarios.

Refund tracking ensures accurate financial reporting and prevents over-refunding beyond the original transaction value.

payment_details.description:
JSON string containing encrypted payment details for PCI DSS compliance.

Stores sensitive payment information in encrypted format, including tokenized card data, billing information, and gateway-specific metadata. The encryption ensures payment security while preserving necessary transaction details.

Proper tokenization and encryption maintain PCI DSS compliance while enabling successful transaction processing and customer service operations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment record was created in the system.

Records the initial creation date and time of the payment transaction. Uses ISO 8601 format for consistent timestamp representation across all system components.

The creation timestamp establishes the starting point for payment lifecycle tracking and audit trail maintenance.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last update to the payment record.

Tracks the most recent modification date and time for the payment transaction. Updates occur for status changes, refund processing, dispute handling, and administrative corrections.

The update timestamp provides visibility into payment activity and supports accurate audit trail maintenance.

order.description:
Order associated with this payment transaction.

Provides complete context about the order that this payment is associated with. The order summary includes essential information such as order number, customer details, order status, and financial totals.

This reference enables complete payment information retrieval in a single API call, eliminating the need for additional order lookup operations and providing full payment context for administrative and customer service purposes.

IShoppingMallPayment.description:
Payment transaction entity representing complete financial transactions associated with shopping mall orders.

Manages all payment processing for orders including authorization, capture, refunds, and chargebacks. Each payment record tracks the complete financial transaction lifecycle with secure payment gateway integration. Payments support multiple methods (credit cards, PayPal, bank transfers, digital wallets) and handle complex scenarios like split payments, partial refunds, and dispute resolution.

Payment records maintain PCI DSS compliance by storing only tokenized payment information and maintaining complete audit trails for financial reconciliation. The entity includes comprehensive status tracking, gateway integration details, and financial amounts with proper currency handling.

Includes complete order context for comprehensive information retrieval, enabling single-call payment data access with full order relationship context. This design eliminates the need for additional API calls to retrieve order information, improving performance and user experience.

SECURITY NOTE: Sensitive payment details and authorization codes are properly handled according to PCI DSS standards. The response DTO excludes raw payment information to prevent data exposure while maintaining necessary transaction details for business operations.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starting from 1). Used to navigate through large result sets efficiently.

limit.description: Number of items per page for pagination. Controls the size of result batches returned to the client.

search.description: Search query to filter payments by transaction ID, payment method, or gateway reference. Supports partial matching for flexible search capabilities.

oneOf.description: Filter payments by specific status to focus on particular stages of the payment lifecycle. Valid values include pending authorization, captured transactions, declined payments, refunded amounts, disputed transactions, and chargeback cases.

IShoppingMallPayment.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for payment filtering operations.

Provides comprehensive search capabilities for payment records linked to a particular order. Supports complex filtering by payment status, method, transaction ID, date ranges, and gateway references. Includes pagination controls for efficient data retrieval and sorting options for organized result presentation.

This request DTO enables sophisticated payment search functionality while maintaining performance through proper pagination and filtering. Used in payment search operations to help users find specific payment transactions matching their criteria across the complete payment lifecycle from authorization through settlement and potential disputes.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the payment record. Generated automatically upon payment creation using UUID v4 for global uniqueness.

order.description: Order associated with this payment transaction. Provides essential context for understanding the payment's business purpose and customer relationship.

payment_method.description: Payment method used for the transaction. Indicates the channel through which the payment was processed (credit card, PayPal, bank transfer, digital wallet).

payment_gateway.description: Payment gateway service used for processing the transaction. Identifies the specific payment processor responsible for authorization and settlement.

transaction_id.description: Unique transaction identifier from the payment gateway. Used for reconciliation with external payment systems and audit trail purposes.

amount.description: Total amount processed for this payment. Represents the financial value of the transaction in the specified currency.

currency.description: Currency code used for the payment. Follows ISO 4217 standard for consistent currency representation across the platform.

status.description: Current status of the payment transaction. Tracks the payment lifecycle from authorization through capture, refund, or dispute resolution.

authorization_code.description: Payment authorization code from the gateway. Provides reference for transaction verification and potential refund or dispute resolution.

captured_at.description: Timestamp when payment was successfully captured and funds were transferred. Indicates completion of the payment settlement process.

refunded_amount.description: Total amount refunded for this payment. Tracks partial or full refunds processed against the original transaction.

payment_details.description: JSON string containing encrypted payment details. Stores sensitive payment information securely for audit and reconciliation purposes.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the payment record was created. Marks the initiation of the payment transaction process.

updated_at.description: Last payment update timestamp. Tracks modifications to payment status, refund amounts, or other payment attributes.

IShoppingMallPayment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of payment transactions for list displays and overview purposes.

Provides essential payment information including the associated order context for complete transaction understanding. Suitable for displaying payment history, transaction lists, and payment status overviews where full payment details are not required.

This summary format ensures secure display of payment information while maintaining compliance with data protection regulations. Includes order reference for contextual understanding of payment transactions without requiring additional API calls. The summary captures the complete payment lifecycle from authorization through potential refunds and disputes, providing comprehensive transaction visibility for customer service and administrative purposes.

IShoppingMallPayment.ICreate.description:
Payment creation DTO for initiating new payment transactions.

Contains all required information to create a payment record for an order. This DTO focuses on the initial payment setup including method selection, gateway configuration, transaction initialization, and payment status assignment. The creation process establishes the foundation for payment authorization and capture workflows.

Security considerations require that sensitive payment information is properly handled according to PCI DSS standards. The DTO excludes system-generated fields and focuses on user-provided payment configuration details necessary for transaction processing.

Used exclusively for payment creation operations where authorized users initiate payment processing for existing orders. The DTO ensures all mandatory payment parameters are provided while maintaining proper separation of payment processing responsibilities.

Note: The order context is provided via the path parameter /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderId}/payments and should not be duplicated in the request body. Payment status is required at creation to properly initialize the payment lifecycle state.

This DTO maps directly to the shopping_mall_payments Prisma schema, ensuring complete field coverage and type compatibility with the underlying database structure.

oneOf.description:
Payment method to be used for the transaction.

Specifies the payment method for processing the transaction. Must be one of the supported values: credit_card, paypal, bank_transfer, digital_wallet. The method determines the processing workflow, validation rules, and gateway requirements.

Method selection influences customer experience, security requirements, and transaction processing timelines. Each method has specific implementation considerations and compliance requirements that must be addressed during payment creation.

Credit card payments require PCI DSS compliance and tokenization of sensitive card data. PayPal payments involve redirect flows and API integration. Bank transfers require account verification and clearing time considerations. Digital wallets provide convenience but have specific platform requirements.

payment_gateway.description:
Payment gateway to be used for processing.

Identifies the specific payment gateway service that will handle this transaction. Gateway selection may be based on payment method compatibility, currency support, regional availability, or business preferences.

The gateway determines the communication protocol, security standards, and processing capabilities available for the payment transaction. Proper gateway configuration is essential for successful payment processing.

Common gateway examples include Stripe, PayPal, Square, and Adyen. Gateway selection impacts transaction fees, processing speed, and customer experience. The gateway must support the selected payment method and currency.

transaction_id.description:
Unique transaction identifier from the payment gateway.

External identifier provided by the payment gateway that will uniquely identify this transaction. This ID is required for cross-referencing and reconciliation with external payment systems.

The transaction ID serves as the primary reference for communication with payment processors and is essential for dispute resolution, chargeback handling, and financial reconciliation.

Transaction IDs typically follow gateway-specific formats and may include prefixes or suffixes indicating the transaction type or processing environment. The ID must be unique within the gateway's system to prevent conflicts.

amount.description:
Payment amount to be processed.

The monetary value of the payment transaction. Must be a positive number representing the total amount to be charged to the customer. Amount validation includes checking for minimum/maximum limits and currency-specific formatting.

The amount determines the financial value of the transaction and influences processing fees, gateway selection, and regulatory reporting requirements.

Amounts must be expressed in the specified currency with appropriate decimal precision. The system validates that the amount does not exceed order limits and complies with business rules for transaction size restrictions.

currency.description:
Currency code for the payment transaction.

Standard three-letter ISO 4217 currency code specifying the currency for the payment. Examples include USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, etc. Currency selection affects exchange rates, formatting, and regional compliance.

The currency must be supported by the selected payment gateway and comply with business rules for international transactions and financial reporting.

Currency validation ensures that the payment amount is processed correctly and that exchange rate calculations are accurate. The currency must match the order currency to maintain financial consistency.

oneOf.description:
Initial payment status indicating the transaction is awaiting processing.

Sets the payment to pending status, indicating that the transaction has been initiated but not yet processed by the payment gateway. Pending status is appropriate for payments that require additional verification or manual approval.

Pending payments may transition to authorized, declined, or other statuses based on gateway response and business rules. This status provides flexibility for complex payment workflows and manual intervention requirements.

Payment status indicating successful authorization without capture.

Sets the payment to authorized status, indicating that the payment gateway has approved the transaction but funds have not yet been captured. Authorized status is common for credit card transactions where capture occurs later.

Authorized payments can be captured to complete the transaction or voided to cancel the authorization. This status supports delayed capture workflows and provides payment assurance without immediate fund transfer.

Payment status indicating successful capture of authorized funds.

Sets the payment to captured status, indicating that funds have been successfully transferred from the customer to the merchant. Capture status represents completed payment transactions ready for order fulfillment.

Captured payments are considered final unless refunds or disputes occur. This status triggers order processing workflows and updates inventory and accounting systems accordingly.

Payment status indicating gateway rejection of the transaction.

Sets the payment to declined status, indicating that the payment gateway has rejected the transaction due to insufficient funds, security concerns, or other validation failures.

Declined payments require customer notification and alternative payment method selection. This status prevents order processing and maintains accurate payment failure tracking for analytics and customer service.

Payment status indicating full or partial refund processing.

Sets the payment to refunded status, indicating that funds have been returned to the customer. Refunds may be partial or full based on business requirements and customer agreements.

Refunded status supports customer satisfaction and dispute resolution workflows. The status includes tracking of refund amounts and maintains audit trails for financial reconciliation.

Payment status indicating customer dispute initiation.

Sets the payment to disputed status, indicating that the customer has initiated a formal dispute through their payment provider. Disputed status triggers investigation workflows and documentation requirements.

Disputed payments require careful handling to resolve customer concerns while protecting merchant rights. This status supports chargeback prevention and customer relationship management.

Payment status indicating formal chargeback processing.

Sets the payment to chargeback status, indicating that the payment provider has reversed the transaction due to a successful dispute. Chargebacks represent financial losses and require documentation for potential recovery.

Chargeback status supports financial reporting and loss prevention analysis. The status helps identify patterns and improve payment processing practices to reduce future chargebacks.

status.description:
Initial payment status for the transaction.

Specifies the starting status of the payment lifecycle. Must be one of the supported values: pending, authorized, captured, declined, refunded, disputed, chargeback. The status determines the initial workflow state and available transitions.

Status selection influences payment processing behavior, customer communication, and financial tracking. Each status has specific business rules and operational implications that must be considered during payment creation.

The status must align with the payment method and gateway capabilities. For example, credit card payments typically start with authorized status, while bank transfers may start with pending status awaiting clearing.

authorization_code.description:
Payment authorization code if pre-authorized.

Optional authorization code provided by the payment gateway if the payment has been pre-authorized. This code is required for capture operations and serves as proof of initial authorization.

Inclusion of an authorization code indicates that the payment has already passed the authorization phase and is ready for capture, streamlining the payment processing workflow.

Authorization codes are typically alphanumeric strings provided by payment gateways during the authorization process. The code must be stored securely and referenced during capture operations to ensure transaction integrity.

payment_details.description:
JSON string containing encrypted payment details.

Stores sensitive payment information in encrypted format for PCI DSS compliance. The JSON structure includes tokenized payment data, billing information, and gateway-specific metadata required for transaction processing.

Proper encryption and tokenization ensure payment security while preserving the information needed for successful transaction processing and customer service operations.

The JSON structure must follow gateway-specific formats and include all necessary elements for payment processing, dispute resolution, and customer verification. Encryption standards must meet PCI DSS requirements for data protection.

IShoppingMallPayment.IUpdate.description:
Payment update DTO for modifying existing payment transactions.

Allows authorized users to update payment details for administrative purposes, correction handling, or status management. The update operation supports modifying payment status, refund amounts, authorization codes, and capture timestamps while maintaining financial integrity.

Security considerations require that payment updates are carefully controlled to prevent unauthorized modifications to financial records. The DTO excludes immutable fields and focuses on modifiable payment attributes that support proper financial workflows.

Used for administrative payment management where authorized users need to correct payment information, update status based on external events, or handle payment disputes and chargebacks through proper status transitions.

This DTO supports partial updates through optional fields, allowing administrators to modify specific payment attributes without requiring complete payment reconfiguration. All updates maintain audit trails and financial compliance requirements.

The DTO maps to the shopping_mall_payments Prisma schema, ensuring that updates maintain database integrity and support comprehensive payment lifecycle management across the shopping mall platform.

oneOf.description:
Updated payment method for the transaction.

Optional field allowing modification of the payment method if the original method needs correction or if the payment method changes during processing. Method changes may require additional validation and gateway reconfiguration.

Payment method updates are typically used for administrative corrections or when customers request payment method changes after initial transaction setup.

Method updates must comply with gateway capabilities and business rules. Changing payment methods may require reprocessing the transaction through the new payment gateway with appropriate authorization and capture workflows.

payment_gateway.description:
Updated payment gateway for processing.

Optional field allowing modification of the payment gateway if gateway changes are required due to service issues, regional requirements, or business decisions. Gateway changes may involve transaction migration or reprocessing.

Gateway updates are administrative operations that require careful handling to maintain transaction consistency and financial integrity across payment processing systems.

Gateway changes may be necessary when switching payment processors, addressing regional restrictions, or optimizing transaction costs. The new gateway must support the payment method and currency configuration.

transaction_id.description:
Updated transaction identifier from the gateway.

Optional field allowing correction of the transaction ID if the original identifier was incorrect or if the transaction needs to be reassigned to a different gateway transaction.

Transaction ID updates are typically used for administrative corrections when gateway communication issues result in incorrect transaction references.

Transaction ID corrections ensure proper reconciliation with external payment systems and support accurate financial reporting. The updated ID must be valid within the payment gateway's system to maintain transaction integrity.

oneOf.description:
Updated payment status indicating the transaction is awaiting processing.

Modifies the payment status to pending, typically used for administrative corrections or when reprocessing is required. Pending status indicates that the transaction requires additional processing or verification.

Status updates to pending may be used when resetting payment workflows or addressing processing delays. The status change triggers appropriate notification and workflow management processes.

Updated payment status indicating successful authorization without capture.

Modifies the payment status to authorized, typically used when correcting status errors or when authorization occurs after initial payment creation. Authorized status indicates gateway approval with pending capture.

Status updates to authorized support payment workflow corrections and ensure accurate financial tracking. The status change may require additional authorization code validation and capture scheduling.

Updated payment status indicating successful capture of authorized funds.

Modifies the payment status to captured, typically used when correcting status errors or when capture occurs through alternative processes. Captured status indicates completed fund transfer.

Status updates to captured finalize payment transactions and trigger order fulfillment workflows. The status change requires validation of capture completion and financial reconciliation.

Updated payment status indicating gateway rejection of the transaction.

Modifies the payment status to declined, typically used for administrative corrections or when decline information is received after initial processing. Declined status prevents order fulfillment.

Status updates to declined support accurate payment failure tracking and customer communication. The status change may include decline reason documentation for customer service purposes.

Updated payment status indicating full or partial refund processing.

Modifies the payment status to refunded, typically used when processing refunds through administrative interfaces or when correcting refund status errors. Refunded status indicates fund return to customer.

Status updates to refunded support customer satisfaction and financial reconciliation. The status change requires validation of refund amounts and compliance with refund policies.

Updated payment status indicating customer dispute initiation.

Modifies the payment status to disputed, typically used when receiving dispute notifications from payment processors or when correcting dispute status errors. Disputed status triggers investigation workflows.

Status updates to disputed support proper dispute management and customer service response. The status change requires documentation of dispute details and communication records.

Updated payment status indicating formal chargeback processing.

Modifies the payment status to chargeback, typically used when receiving chargeback notifications or when correcting chargeback status errors. Chargeback status indicates financial reversal.

Status updates to chargeback support financial reporting and loss prevention analysis. The status change requires documentation of chargeback details and potential recovery efforts.

status.description:
Updated payment status for the transaction.

Optional field allowing modification of the payment status to reflect changes in the payment lifecycle. Status transitions must follow business rules and regulatory requirements for proper financial tracking.

Status updates are essential for handling payment disputes, chargebacks, refunds, and other payment lifecycle events that require official status changes for audit and reporting purposes.

Status transitions must comply with payment gateway capabilities and business workflow rules. For example, captured payments cannot revert to authorized status, and refunded payments require proper authorization and documentation.

authorization_code.description:
Updated authorization code for the payment.

Optional field allowing correction or update of the authorization code if the original code was incorrect or if reauthorization occurs. Authorization code updates ensure proper reference to gateway authorization records.

Code updates support payment correction workflows and ensure accurate financial reconciliation with payment processors.

Authorization code corrections may be necessary when gateway communication errors result in incorrect code storage or when multiple authorization attempts occur. The updated code must be valid within the payment gateway's system.

captured_at.description:
Updated capture timestamp for the payment.

Optional field allowing correction of the capture timestamp if the original timestamp was inaccurate or if capture occurs at a different time than initially recorded.

Capture timestamp updates ensure accurate financial reporting and proper sequencing of payment events for audit and reconciliation purposes.

Timestamp corrections support accurate financial reporting and compliance with accounting standards. The updated timestamp must reflect the actual capture event time and maintain chronological consistency with other payment events.

refunded_amount.description:
Updated refund amount for the payment.

Optional field allowing modification of the refund amount to reflect partial or additional refunds processed for the payment. Refund amount updates must not exceed the original payment amount.

Refund amount tracking ensures accurate financial reporting, prevents over-refunding, and maintains proper audit trails for customer dispute resolution.

Refund amount updates support customer service operations and financial reconciliation. The updated amount must comply with refund policies and maintain consistency with actual refund transactions processed through the payment gateway.

payment_details.description:
Updated encrypted payment details.

Optional field allowing correction or update of payment details if the original information was incomplete, inaccurate, or requires updates for processing or customer service purposes.

Payment detail updates support administrative corrections and ensure accurate payment information for transaction processing and customer service operations.

Detail updates may be necessary when correcting billing information, updating tokenized payment data, or addressing gateway-specific metadata requirements. The updated details must maintain PCI DSS compliance and data security standards.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the shipment record. Generated automatically using UUID v4 format to ensure global uniqueness across all shipment records in the system.

Used as the primary reference for shipment operations and database relationships. This identifier remains constant throughout the shipment lifecycle and cannot be modified after creation.

order.description:
Reference to the order being shipped, providing complete context about the associated customer purchase.

Contains essential order information including order number, total amount, currency, and current status. This relationship ensures proper linkage between shipments and their corresponding orders for accurate fulfillment tracking.

The order reference maintains data integrity by preventing orphaned shipments and enabling comprehensive order-shipment relationship management throughout the delivery process.

carrier.description:
Shipping carrier responsible for package delivery and tracking services.

Supported carriers include major logistics providers such as USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL, and other regional delivery services. Carrier selection determines tracking capabilities, delivery timelines, and service level options available for the shipment.

Each carrier maintains specific API integrations for real-time tracking updates and label generation, ensuring seamless integration with the platform's shipping management system.

tracking_number.description:
Unique tracking number assigned by the carrier for shipment monitoring and customer tracking.

This identifier follows carrier-specific formats and provides the primary reference for tracking package movement through the delivery network. Tracking numbers are validated against carrier systems to ensure accuracy and prevent duplication.

Customers use this number to monitor delivery progress through carrier tracking portals and receive real-time updates on shipment status and estimated delivery times.

shipping_method.description:
Shipping service level selected for the delivery, determining speed and cost.

Available methods include standard ground shipping, expedited delivery, overnight service, and international options. Each method corresponds to specific delivery timelines and pricing structures based on carrier capabilities.

The selected method impacts delivery speed, cost calculations, and customer expectations regarding receipt timing. Method selection is validated against carrier availability and order requirements.

shipping_cost.description:
Cost associated with this specific shipment, calculated based on carrier rates and service level.

Represents the actual shipping charge applied to the order, including any surcharges, insurance, or special handling fees. Costs are calculated using carrier rate tables and validated against expected pricing ranges.

This amount contributes to the order's total cost and is reflected in customer billing and financial reporting. Cost accuracy is critical for proper revenue tracking and customer satisfaction.

status.description:
Current status of the shipment within the delivery lifecycle.

Valid status values follow a sequential workflow: label_created (initial state), picked_up (carrier collection), in_transit (package movement), out_for_delivery (local delivery), delivered (final completion).

Status transitions are validated to ensure logical progression and prevent invalid state changes. Each status update triggers customer notifications and system workflow processing for order fulfillment tracking.

estimated_delivery.description:
Estimated delivery date and time provided by the carrier based on shipping method and route.

This projection considers carrier service levels, distance, and operational factors to provide customers with expected delivery timing. Estimates are updated dynamically as the shipment progresses through the delivery network.

Used for customer communication and delivery planning, with accuracy improving as the shipment approaches the destination. Actual delivery timing may vary based on operational conditions.

actual_delivery.description:
Actual timestamp when the package was successfully delivered to the recipient.

Captured through carrier delivery confirmation systems or customer acknowledgment. This timestamp marks the completion of the delivery process and triggers order completion workflows.

Used for performance metrics, delivery verification, and customer service resolution. Delivery confirmation may include recipient signature or electronic acknowledgment based on carrier capabilities.

shipping_label_url.description:
URL providing access to the shipping label document for printing and carrier processing.

Generated through carrier integration systems and containing essential shipping information including addresses, barcodes, and tracking references. Labels follow carrier-specific formats and requirements.

Used by warehouse staff for package preparation and by carriers for scanning and tracking. Label URLs are secured and accessible only to authorized personnel with appropriate permissions.

tracking_url.description:
Direct URL to the carrier's tracking page for real-time shipment monitoring.

Provides customers and administrators with direct access to carrier tracking systems without requiring manual tracking number entry. URLs are carrier-specific and include pre-populated tracking information.

Enables seamless tracking experience and reduces customer support requests by providing immediate access to delivery status updates and estimated timelines.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the shipment record was initially created in the system.

Represents the start of the shipping process and is used for audit trails, reporting, and chronological ordering of shipment activities. This timestamp is automatically generated and cannot be modified.

Used for performance metrics, delivery timeline analysis, and system activity tracking. Creation timing impacts delivery estimates and customer expectation management.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the shipment record, capturing all modifications.

Tracks changes to shipment status, tracking information, delivery estimates, and other critical fields. Each update reflects progress in the delivery lifecycle or correction of shipment details.

Used for change tracking, audit compliance, and real-time status monitoring. Frequent updates indicate active shipment movement and carrier system integration.

IShoppingMallShipment.description:
Shipping and delivery information entity for comprehensive order fulfillment tracking.

Tracks the complete shipping lifecycle from label creation through final delivery, providing customers with real-time visibility into package movement and delivery progress. Each shipment represents a physical delivery package associated with a customer order, supporting complex scenarios including split shipments, multiple package deliveries, and international shipping.

Shipments integrate with carrier APIs for automated tracking updates, label generation, and delivery confirmation. The entity maintains carrier-specific information, cost calculations, and delivery timelines to ensure accurate fulfillment tracking and customer communication.

Used across customer-facing tracking interfaces, administrative shipment management, and carrier integration systems. The shipment entity supports multi-carrier operations with standardized tracking while preserving carrier-specific capabilities and service levels.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results retrieval, starting from 1 for the first page.

Controls which subset of shipment records to return when dealing with large result sets. Page-based navigation ensures efficient data retrieval and optimal performance for search operations with extensive filtering criteria.

Combined with the limit parameter, enables controlled data access and prevents overwhelming response sizes while maintaining complete result set accessibility through sequential page requests.

limit.description:
Maximum number of shipment records to include in each page of results.

Limits result set size for performance optimization and user interface manageability. The maximum value of 100 prevents excessive data transfer and processing overhead while providing sufficient records for most search scenarios.

Smaller limits improve response times for large data sets, while larger limits reduce pagination requirements for comprehensive result reviews. Default values typically balance performance and usability requirements.

search.description:
Free-text search query for comprehensive shipment filtering across multiple fields.

Supports partial matching and case-insensitive search across tracking numbers, carrier names, and shipping methods. The search functionality enables quick location of specific shipments without requiring exact field matching.

Ideal for administrative lookup operations and customer service scenarios where precise filtering criteria may not be known. Search results prioritize relevance and include fuzzy matching for common data entry variations.

carrier.description:
Filter shipments by specific carrier name to narrow results to particular logistics providers.

Supported values include major carriers such as USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL, and other configured delivery services. Carrier filtering enables focused management of shipments handled by specific providers.

Useful for carrier performance analysis, service level monitoring, and operational reporting. Combined with other filters, provides granular control over shipment result sets based on delivery partner selection.

min_shipping_cost.description:
Minimum shipping cost filter for financial analysis and cost-based result filtering.

Returns shipments with shipping costs equal to or greater than the specified value. Enables identification of high-value shipments, cost trend analysis, and budgetary monitoring.

Useful for financial reporting, carrier cost comparison, and operational efficiency analysis. Combined with maximum cost filtering, creates precise cost ranges for targeted financial review.

max_shipping_cost.description:
Maximum shipping cost filter for financial control and cost ceiling enforcement.

Returns shipments with shipping costs equal to or less than the specified value. Supports cost containment monitoring, budget adherence verification, and identification of cost outliers.

Essential for financial management, exception reporting, and operational cost optimization. When used with minimum cost filtering, defines specific cost ranges for detailed financial analysis.

min_estimated_delivery.description:
Minimum estimated delivery date filter for timeline-based shipment searching.

Returns shipments with estimated delivery dates on or after the specified timestamp. Enables future delivery planning, capacity forecasting, and delivery timeline analysis.

Useful for operational planning, customer service anticipation, and delivery workload forecasting. Helps identify upcoming deliveries requiring preparation or special handling considerations.

max_estimated_delivery.description:
Maximum estimated delivery date filter for delivery timeline management.

Returns shipments with estimated delivery dates on or before the specified timestamp. Supports delivery performance monitoring, timeline compliance verification, and past delivery analysis.

Essential for service level agreement tracking, delivery performance reporting, and historical trend analysis. Combined with minimum date filtering, creates precise delivery windows for targeted review.

oneOf.description: Sort shipment results by creation timestamp for chronological analysis.
Sort shipment results by estimated delivery date for timeline planning.
Sort shipment results by shipping cost for financial analysis.

order_by.description:
Primary field for sorting shipment search results, determining result ordering.

Available sorting options support different analytical perspectives: created_at for chronological review, estimated_delivery for delivery planning, and shipping_cost for financial analysis.

Sorting enhances result usability by organizing records based on relevant business criteria. Combined with direction parameter, enables both ascending and descending order arrangements for comprehensive data review.

oneOf.description: Ascending sort order (oldest first, earliest delivery, lowest cost).
Descending sort order (newest first, latest delivery, highest cost).

direction.description:
Sorting direction controlling the order of returned shipment records.

Ascending order (asc) arranges records from smallest to largest values, suitable for historical analysis and baseline reporting. Descending order (desc) arranges records from largest to smallest values, ideal for recent activity review and priority identification.

The direction parameter works with order_by to provide flexible result organization tailored to specific analytical needs and user preferences.

IShoppingMallShipment.IRequest.description:
Comprehensive search and filtering criteria for shipment retrieval operations with advanced capabilities.

Provides extensive filtering options for searching through shipment records based on carrier information, delivery status, cost ranges, delivery timelines, and tracking details. Supports sophisticated search scenarios including date range filtering, cost analysis, and status-based operational monitoring.

The request type enables flexible search capabilities while maintaining performance through pagination controls and targeted filtering options. Advanced filtering supports both administrative oversight and customer service scenarios with precise result set control.

Combined with pagination parameters, ensures efficient handling of large data sets while providing granular control over result composition. The comprehensive filtering capabilities support diverse use cases from basic shipment lookup to complex operational analysis and reporting requirements.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the shipment record. Automatically generated UUID v4 that uniquely identifies each shipment in the system. Used for database retrieval and API operations requiring shipment identification.

order.description:
Reference to the order being shipped, providing complete context for shipment tracking.

Contains essential order information including order number, total amount, currency, status, and customer details. This reference ensures proper shipment-to-order relationship mapping while maintaining data integrity and preventing orphaned shipment records.

carrier.description:
Shipping carrier responsible for package delivery and tracking services.

Supported carriers include USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL, and other major logistics providers. Each carrier maintains specific tracking systems and delivery standards that customers can monitor through the provided tracking URLs.

tracking_number.description:
Unique tracking number assigned by the carrier for shipment monitoring.

This identifier enables real-time tracking through carrier APIs and provides customers with delivery progress visibility. Tracking numbers follow carrier-specific formats and are validated against carrier systems during shipment creation.

shipping_method.description:
Shipping service level selected for package delivery.

Available methods include standard ground shipping, expedited delivery, overnight service, and international options. Each method has specific delivery timelines and cost structures that impact the overall shipping experience.

shipping_cost.description:
Cost associated with this specific shipment, calculated based on package weight, dimensions, and selected shipping method.

Represents the actual shipping fee charged to the customer, excluding product costs and taxes. This amount contributes to the order's total shipping calculation and financial reporting.

status.description:
Current status of the shipment lifecycle from creation through final delivery.

Valid status values include: label_created (initial state), picked_up (carrier collected), in_transit (package moving), out_for_delivery (local delivery), delivered (successful completion). Each status transition triggers customer notifications and system updates.

estimated_delivery.description:
Estimated delivery date provided by the carrier based on shipping method and destination.

This projection helps customers anticipate package arrival and plan accordingly. Estimates may be updated by carriers based on actual transit progress and external factors affecting delivery timelines.

actual_delivery.description:
Actual timestamp when the package was successfully delivered to the recipient.

Captured through carrier API integration or manual confirmation. This timestamp marks the completion of the shipment lifecycle and triggers order status updates and customer notifications.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the shipment record was initially created in the system.

Represents the start of the shipment lifecycle and serves as a reference point for tracking shipment duration and performance metrics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the shipment record.

Tracks all modifications including status changes, tracking updates, and delivery confirmations. Provides audit trail for shipment management and customer service inquiries.

IShoppingMallShipment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of shipment information optimized for efficient tracking and overview displays.

Provides essential shipping details suitable for order summaries, shipment lists, and customer tracking dashboards. This summary format excludes sensitive implementation details while maintaining sufficient context for shipment monitoring and management.

The summary includes key carrier information, tracking details, and delivery timelines that customers need to monitor their package progress. By referencing the order summary rather than exposing raw order IDs, this format maintains data integrity while preventing excessive information exposure.

Used primarily in administrative interfaces, customer order history pages, and shipment tracking systems where full shipment details are not required. The compact design ensures optimal performance in list views and search results while maintaining comprehensive shipment context.

carrier.description:
Shipping carrier selection for package delivery services.

Supported carriers include USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL, and other major logistics providers. Each carrier offers specific service levels, tracking capabilities, and delivery networks that impact shipping costs and delivery timelines. Carrier selection must be validated against supported options during shipment creation.

tracking_number.description:
Unique tracking number assigned by the selected carrier for shipment monitoring.

This identifier enables real-time tracking integration with carrier APIs and provides customers with delivery progress visibility. Tracking numbers must follow carrier-specific formats and be validated against carrier systems to ensure accurate tracking functionality.

shipping_method.description:
Shipping service level selection determining delivery speed and cost.

Available methods include standard ground shipping (3-7 business days), expedited delivery (2-3 business days), overnight service (next business day), and international options. Method selection impacts carrier availability, shipping costs, and customer delivery expectations.

shipping_cost.description:
Cost calculation for this specific shipment based on package characteristics.

Determined by package weight, dimensions, destination, and selected shipping method. This cost represents the actual shipping fee charged to the customer and contributes to the order's financial calculations and profit margins.

status.description:
Initial shipment status setting upon creation.

Typically defaults to 'label_created' indicating the shipment record has been initialized but not yet processed by the carrier. Administrators may set alternative initial statuses for special handling scenarios or manual status overrides.

estimated_delivery.description:
Projected delivery date based on carrier service levels and destination.

Provides customers with delivery expectations and helps manage customer communications. This estimate may be refined by carriers based on actual transit progress and operational factors affecting delivery schedules.

shipping_label_url.description:
URL for accessing the shipping label document required for package processing.

Points to the generated shipping label that carriers scan during pickup and processing. Label URLs must be accessible to shipping personnel and integrate with carrier label printing systems for efficient package handling.

tracking_url.description:
URL directing customers to the carrier's tracking page for real-time updates.

Provides direct access to carrier tracking systems where customers can monitor package progress, estimated delivery times, and any delivery exceptions or delays encountered during transit.

IShoppingMallShipment.ICreate.description:
Shipment creation data structure for initiating new shipping records in the shopping mall platform.

Contains all necessary information to create a shipment record including carrier selection, tracking setup, shipping method configuration, and cost calculations. This DTO integrates with carrier systems to validate shipping options and generate tracking capabilities.

The creation process excludes system-managed fields like id, created_at, and updated_at, which are automatically generated. The target order is identified through the API path parameter `/shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderId}/shipments` rather than duplicate order references in the request body.

Optional fields like estimated_delivery, shipping_label_url, and tracking_url provide enhanced shipment functionality when available, while status allows for custom initial state configuration when needed. All field validations ensure shipment records maintain data integrity and carrier compliance standards.

carrier.description:
Shipping carrier responsible for delivery (USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL, etc.). This field identifies the logistics provider handling the shipment and determines tracking capabilities and delivery timelines.

Carrier selection impacts shipping costs, delivery speed, and tracking availability. Valid carriers are configured in the system and must be selected from approved provider lists to ensure proper integration with carrier APIs for real-time tracking updates.

tracking_number.description:
Unique tracking number assigned by the carrier for shipment tracking and monitoring.

This identifier enables customers and administrators to track shipment progress through carrier systems. Tracking numbers must be unique within the system and follow carrier-specific format requirements. The system validates tracking number uniqueness and format compliance during updates.

shipping_method.description:
Shipping service level selected for the delivery (standard, expedited, overnight).

Defines the speed and priority of the shipment delivery. Standard shipping provides economical delivery with longer transit times, while expedited and overnight options offer faster delivery at premium costs. Shipping method selection affects both delivery timelines and shipping costs.

shipping_cost.description:
Cost associated with this specific shipment in the order's currency.

Represents the actual shipping cost charged by the carrier for this shipment. Must be non-negative and reflects the carrier's pricing for the selected shipping method and package characteristics. Shipping costs are calculated based on package weight, dimensions, and destination.

status.description:
Current status of the shipment tracking its delivery lifecycle (label_created, picked_up, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered).

Status transitions follow a predefined workflow: label_created → picked_up → in_transit → out_for_delivery → delivered. Status updates are typically received from carrier APIs and provide real-time visibility into shipment progress. Invalid status transitions are rejected to maintain workflow integrity.

estimated_delivery.description:
Estimated delivery date and time provided by the carrier based on shipping method and destination.

This timestamp represents the carrier's projected delivery timeframe. Estimated delivery dates are calculated using carrier algorithms considering distance, service level, and operational factors. Actual delivery may vary based on weather, traffic, and other external conditions.

actual_delivery.description:
Actual timestamp when the package was successfully delivered to the recipient.

This field is populated automatically when the carrier confirms delivery through their tracking system. Actual delivery timestamps provide precise completion records for order fulfillment tracking and customer service purposes. Once set, this field cannot be modified.

shipping_label_url.description:
URL to download the shipping label document for printing and carrier processing.

Shipping labels contain essential information for carriers including recipient address, package details, and barcodes for scanning. Label URLs are generated by the shipping system and provide secure access to printable label documents. Labels expire after a configured period for security.

tracking_url.description:
Direct URL to the carrier's tracking page for real-time shipment monitoring.

This link provides customers with direct access to carrier tracking systems for detailed shipment progress information. Tracking URLs are dynamically generated based on carrier and tracking number to ensure accurate redirection to the appropriate carrier tracking interface.

IShoppingMallShipment.IUpdate.description:
Updated shipment information including carrier details, tracking, and delivery status for order fulfillment management.

This DTO allows authorized administrators to modify shipment properties while maintaining data integrity and workflow compliance. All fields are optional to support partial updates, enabling granular modifications without requiring complete object replacement.

The DTO excludes immutable fields such as shipment ID, creation timestamps, and order references to prevent unauthorized modifications. Status transitions are validated server-side to ensure they follow proper workflow sequences (e.g., cannot revert from delivered status).

Security enforcement ensures that only authorized administrators with appropriate permissions can update shipments, with additional validation to confirm users have access to the associated order. The system automatically tracks update timestamps and maintains audit trails for compliance purposes.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the coupon record, automatically generated using UUID v4.

This unique identifier provides the primary reference for coupon operations and relationships. The ID is immutable and serves as the internal system reference for coupon management, tracking, and audit purposes.

code.description:
Unique uppercase alphanumeric coupon code that customers enter during checkout for discount application.

Coupon codes must be unique across the platform and follow strict formatting requirements: uppercase letters and numbers only, no special characters. Codes are designed for easy customer entry while maintaining uniqueness constraints for proper coupon identification.

name.description:
Descriptive name for the coupon used for administrative identification and reporting.

Provides human-readable identification for coupon management interfaces. Names should clearly indicate the coupon's purpose, target audience, or promotion type to facilitate easy administration and reporting.

description.description:
Detailed description explaining coupon terms, conditions, eligibility criteria, and usage restrictions.

This comprehensive description provides both administrators and customers with clear understanding of coupon applicability, limitations, and business rules. Descriptions should cover all relevant terms to prevent misuse and ensure proper coupon application.

discount_type.description:
Type of discount offered by the coupon: percentage, fixed_amount, or free_shipping.

Percentage discounts reduce order totals by a specified percentage, fixed_amount discounts subtract a specific monetary amount, and free_shipping discounts waive shipping costs. Discount type determines how the coupon value is applied during checkout calculations.

discount_value.description:
Discount amount or percentage value applied when the coupon is used.

For percentage discounts, this value represents the percentage reduction (e.g., 10 for 10% off). For fixed_amount discounts, this is the monetary reduction amount. Must be positive and validated against order totals to ensure meaningful discount application.

minimum_order_amount.description:
Minimum order amount required to use this coupon, ensuring discounts apply only to qualifying purchases.

This threshold prevents coupon misuse on small-value orders. When specified, the coupon can only be applied to orders meeting or exceeding this amount. Optional field that provides additional control over coupon applicability.

maximum_discount.description:
Maximum discount amount cap for percentage-based coupons to prevent excessive discounts.

For percentage discounts, this field limits the maximum monetary value of the discount regardless of order size. This protects against revenue loss on high-value orders while still providing meaningful savings on typical purchases.

usage_limit_per_customer.description:
Maximum number of times a single customer can use this coupon, preventing abuse and ensuring fair distribution.

This limit controls coupon usage at the customer level to prevent individuals from exploiting unlimited coupon benefits. When reached, the customer cannot apply the coupon to additional orders.

total_usage_limit.description:
Overall maximum usage limit for this coupon across all customers, controlling total platform exposure.

This global limit ensures the coupon's financial impact remains within budgeted parameters. Once the total usage count reaches this limit, the coupon becomes inactive and cannot be applied to new orders.

used_count.description:
Current usage count tracking how many times this coupon has been successfully applied to orders.

This counter provides real-time visibility into coupon utilization for reporting and limit enforcement. The system automatically increments this value each time the coupon is successfully applied during checkout.

valid_from.description:
Date and time when the coupon becomes active and available for use.

Coupons cannot be applied before this timestamp. This allows administrators to schedule coupon availability in advance for promotional campaigns and ensures coupons are only active during intended timeframes.

valid_until.description:
Date and time when the coupon expires and becomes inactive.

After this timestamp, the coupon cannot be applied to new orders regardless of other conditions. Expiration ensures coupons have finite lifetimes and prevents indefinite coupon availability.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether the coupon is currently active and available for customer use.

This flag provides manual control over coupon availability independent of validity periods. Administrators can temporarily deactivate coupons without deleting them, allowing for quick response to issues or campaign adjustments.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the coupon record was created in the system.

Provides audit trail information for coupon lifecycle tracking. This timestamp is automatically set during coupon creation and remains immutable throughout the coupon's existence.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the coupon configuration or properties.

Tracks modification history for audit purposes. This field is automatically updated whenever coupon properties are modified, providing visibility into configuration changes over time.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the coupon was soft deleted for data retention and archival purposes.

Supports soft deletion functionality, allowing coupon removal without permanent data loss. Deleted coupons are excluded from active operations but remain accessible for reporting and audit requirements.

shopping_mall_channel_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the channel where this coupon is valid and applicable.

When specified, restricts coupon usage to orders placed through the designated channel. Provides channel-specific coupon targeting for segmented marketing campaigns and channel-specific promotions.

shopping_mall_administrator_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the administrator who created this coupon.

Maintains creator attribution for audit and responsibility tracking. This relationship ensures proper accountability for coupon creation and configuration.

shopping_mall_administrator_session_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the administrator session when this coupon was created.

Provides detailed audit trail information including the specific session context during coupon creation. This enhances security auditing and supports detailed investigation capabilities.

channel.description:
Channel entity where this coupon is valid and can be applied to orders.

Provides complete channel context including channel name, description, and configuration. This relationship enables channel-specific coupon targeting and ensures coupons are only applicable to appropriate shopping contexts.

creator.description:
Administrator entity who created and configured this coupon.

Provides complete creator information including administrator name, contact details, and role. This relationship supports proper attribution and accountability for coupon management operations.

IShoppingMallCoupon.description:
Platform-managed discount coupons for customer purchases with comprehensive configuration and tracking capabilities.

Coupons represent promotional discount mechanisms that customers can apply during checkout to reduce order totals. Each coupon supports various discount types including percentage-based reductions, fixed amount deductions, and free shipping offers. Coupons are configured with eligibility criteria, validity periods, and usage limits to control their application and financial impact.

The system enforces coupon rules during checkout validation, ensuring discounts are applied only to qualifying orders that meet minimum amount requirements and other conditions. Coupon usage is tracked at both individual customer and platform levels to prevent abuse and maintain promotional budget control.

Administrators manage coupons through comprehensive configuration interfaces, setting discount parameters, eligibility rules, and activation schedules. Coupons can be targeted to specific customer segments, product categories, or shopping channels for precise promotional targeting. The system maintains complete audit trails including creator information, modification history, and usage statistics for reporting and compliance purposes.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starting from 1). Used to navigate through large result sets with configurable page sizes.

limit.description: Number of items per page (maximum 100). Controls the size of each pagination batch for optimal performance.

search.description: Search query to filter coupons by code or name. Supports partial matching and case-insensitive text search.

discount_type.description: Filter by specific discount type: percentage, fixed_amount, free_shipping. Allows filtering coupons by their discount mechanism.

is_active.description: Filter by active status. Shows only currently active coupons or includes inactive ones based on boolean value.

valid_from_min.description: Minimum valid from date filter. Finds coupons that become active on or after this date.

valid_from_max.description: Maximum valid from date filter. Finds coupons that become active on or before this date.

valid_until_min.description: Minimum valid until date filter. Finds coupons that expire on or after this date.

valid_until_max.description: Maximum valid until date filter. Finds coupons that expire on or before this date.

channel_id.description: Filter by specific shopping mall channel ID. Restricts results to coupons valid only in the specified channel.

creator_id.description: Filter by administrator who created the coupon. Useful for audit trails and administrative reporting.

usage_limit_per_customer.description: Filter by customer-specific usage limit. Finds coupons with specific per-customer usage restrictions.

total_usage_limit.description: Filter by overall usage limit. Identifies coupons with specific total usage caps across all customers.

used_count_min.description: Minimum usage count filter. Finds coupons that have been used at least this many times.

used_count_max.description: Maximum usage count filter. Finds coupons that have been used at most this many times.

oneOf.description: Sort results by coupon creation timestamp for chronological ordering.
Sort results by coupon activation date for validity period ordering.
Sort results by coupon expiration date for expiration timeline ordering.
Sort results by discount amount for value-based ordering.
Sort results by usage count for popularity-based ordering.

order_by.description: Field to sort results by. Determines the primary ordering criteria for search results.

oneOf.description: Sort direction: ascending order from smallest to largest values.
Sort direction: descending order from largest to smallest values.

order_direction.description: Sort direction: ascending or descending. Controls the ordering sequence of search results.

IShoppingMallCoupon.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for coupon filtering.

Provides comprehensive filtering options for searching coupons including discount type, validity period, active status, usage statistics, and administrative context. Supports pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting by various coupon properties.

The search functionality allows filtering by coupon code or name using text search with partial matching capabilities. Date range filters enable finding coupons valid within specific time periods, while usage statistics filters help identify popular or underutilized coupons.

Administrative filtering options include channel-specific restrictions and creator-based filtering for audit purposes. The operation supports complex filtering logic with multiple conditions combined using AND/OR operators for precise result targeting.

code.description: Unique coupon code that customers enter during checkout. Must be uppercase and alphanumeric. Generated automatically by the system to ensure uniqueness across the platform.

name.description: Descriptive name for the coupon for administrative purposes. Helps administrators identify and manage coupons effectively.

description.description: Detailed description explaining coupon terms and conditions. Provides customers with clear information about coupon eligibility and usage rules.

discount_type.description: Type of discount: percentage, fixed_amount, free_shipping. Determines how the discount is calculated when applied to orders.

discount_value.description: Discount amount or percentage value. Must be positive. For percentage discounts, represents the percentage reduction; for fixed amounts, represents the dollar value reduction.

minimum_order_amount.description: Minimum order amount required to use this coupon. Ensures coupons are only applied to qualifying orders that meet the minimum threshold.

maximum_discount.description: Maximum discount amount for percentage-based coupons. Prevents excessive discounts on high-value orders while maintaining percentage-based calculations.

usage_limit_per_customer.description: Maximum times a single customer can use this coupon. Controls coupon usage per customer to prevent abuse and ensure fair distribution.

total_usage_limit.description: Overall maximum usage limit for this coupon. Sets a cap on total redemptions across all customers to manage promotional budgets.

valid_from.description: Date and time when coupon becomes active. Coupons cannot be used before this timestamp.

valid_until.description: Date and time when coupon expires. Coupons cannot be used after this timestamp.

is_active.description: Whether the coupon is currently active for use. Inactive coupons are visible but cannot be applied to orders.

shopping_mall_channel_id.description: Channel where this coupon is valid. References the specific shopping mall channel that can use this coupon.

IShoppingMallCoupon.ICreate.description:
Coupon creation parameters including discount configuration, validity period, and usage limits.

This DTO is used when creating new coupons in the shopping mall platform with comprehensive configuration options for discount behavior, eligibility criteria, and promotional controls. The system supports various discount types including percentage-based discounts, fixed amount reductions, and free shipping offers.

Security considerations ensure that administrative context (creator information) is automatically populated from authentication context rather than being accepted from request bodies, maintaining proper audit trails. The coupon code must be unique across the platform and follows uppercase alphanumeric format requirements.

Business logic includes validation of minimum order amounts, maximum discount caps for percentage-based coupons, and proper configuration of customer-specific and overall usage limits. The operation sets default values for tracking fields and ensures proper timestamp recording for audit purposes.

name.description:
Descriptive name for the coupon used for administrative identification and reporting.

This field allows administrators to update the coupon's display name for better management and tracking.
The name should clearly identify the coupon's purpose and target audience for easy reference.

description.description:
Detailed explanation of coupon terms, conditions, and promotional context.

Provides comprehensive information about coupon eligibility rules, redemption conditions, and any special terms.
This description is displayed to administrators and may be shown to customers during coupon application.

discount_type.description:
Type of discount mechanism applied by this coupon.

Valid values include: percentage (percentage-based discount), fixed_amount (fixed monetary discount), 
and free_shipping (waived shipping costs). Each discount type has specific validation requirements
and calculation methods that must be consistent with the discount_value field.

discount_value.description:
Numerical value representing the discount amount or percentage.

For percentage discounts, this value represents the percentage rate (e.g., 10 for 10% discount).
For fixed amount discounts, this value represents the monetary discount in the platform's base currency.
Must be a positive value greater than zero to ensure valid discount application.

minimum_order_amount.description:
Minimum order subtotal required for coupon eligibility.

Specifies the threshold order amount that must be met before the coupon can be applied.
This field helps target coupons to specific customer spending levels and prevents coupon
abuse on very small orders. If null, no minimum order amount restriction applies.

maximum_discount.description:
Maximum discount cap for percentage-based coupons.

Limits the total discount amount when using percentage-based discounts to prevent excessive
coupon value on high-priced items. Only applicable when discount_type is 'percentage'.
If null, no maximum discount cap is enforced for percentage-based coupons.

usage_limit_per_customer.description:
Maximum number of times a single customer can use this coupon.

Helps prevent coupon abuse by limiting individual customer usage while still allowing
broader distribution. If null, customers can use the coupon unlimited times within
the validity period, subject to overall usage limits.

total_usage_limit.description:
Overall maximum usage limit for this coupon across all customers.

Controls the total number of times this coupon can be redeemed system-wide.
This limit helps manage promotional budgets and ensures coupon availability
is controlled according to marketing strategy. If null, no overall usage limit applies.

valid_from.description:
Start date and time when the coupon becomes active and redeemable.

Coupons cannot be applied to orders placed before this timestamp.
The system validates that valid_from is before valid_until and that
both dates are in the future when creating new coupons.

valid_until.description:
Expiration date and time when the coupon becomes inactive.

Coupons cannot be applied to orders placed after this timestamp.
The system automatically deactivates coupons that have passed their
valid_until date, regardless of their is_active status.

is_active.description:
Activation status controlling whether the coupon can be used.

When false, the coupon cannot be applied to any orders even if within
the validity period. This allows administrators to temporarily disable
coupons without deleting them or modifying their configuration.

channel.description:
Shopping channel where this coupon is valid and applicable.

Coupons can be restricted to specific shopping channels to target
particular market segments or geographic regions. If null, the coupon
is valid across all shopping channels in the platform.

IShoppingMallCoupon.IUpdate.description:
Coupon update data transfer object for modifying existing coupon configurations.

This DTO supports partial updates to coupon properties, allowing administrators to modify specific aspects of coupon configuration without requiring complete object replacement. All fields are optional to enable granular updates that maintain data integrity while minimizing the risk of unintended changes.
